escalation.rationale: Score holds near yesterday's high as Russian guided-bomb kills 30 on civilian buses in eastern Ukraine, Iran tanker attacks surge oil prices, Houthis strike Riyadh airport grounding international flights, and South Korea recalls its Ukraine ambassador over North Korean POW disclosure, fracturing a key allied coalition.

ticker_items: Russian guided bomb kills 30 civilians on packed city buses in eastern Ukraine.
Ukraine strikes Omsk Gazprom Neft refinery, Russia's largest, ~2,500 km from border.
Houthis hit Riyadh airport; Lufthansa and Air India suspend Saudi flights.
South Korea recalls ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW disclosure row.
Oil surges on Iran tanker attacks; US gas prices up 46% from pre-war levels.

new_entrant.text: Syria is reportedly weighing deployment of up to 20,000 troops to Yemen to support Saudi-backed operations against the Houthis, which would mark a significant new ground force entry into the Yemen theater.

eastern_europe.description: Russian guided bomb struck public buses filled with passengers at a civilian bus stop, killing at least 30 people.
Ukrainian forces struck the Gazprom Neft-operated Omsk oil refinery, Russia's largest, which supplies fuel to the Russian military.
Russian armed forces struck a cargo ship delivering supplies to Ukrainian forces at Chernomorsk port, according to the Russian MoD.

middle_east.description: Houthi forces struck Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, causing a plane to billow smoke and prompting Lufthansa and Air India to suspend flights to Saudi Arabia.
Escalating tanker attacks in the Gulf attributed to Iran-linked forces drove crude oil to its biggest single-day gain in a month.
Al Jazeera casualty tracker confirms cumulative death toll from US-Israel attacks on Iran at approximately 3,468 in Iran and 3,696 in Lebanon since conflict onset.
UN peacekeeping force UNIFIL reported small arms fire targeting an Israeli border post in Lebanon; no casualties recorded.

observers.description: A Congressional Budget Office report confirmed at least 81 US aircraft worth up to $3.3 billion lost or damaged in the Iran war. President Trump ruled out a new Iran strike before November midterms while Secretary of State Rubio warned Russia's Ukraine war risks broader regional spillover and pressed NATO allies on defense spending.

Seoul recalled its ambassador to Ukraine after Kyiv publicly revealed the secret transfer of two captured North Korean soldiers to South Korea, which Seoul deemed a breach of a non-disclosure agreement. South Korea had demanded an apology it considered insufficiently contrite before taking the diplomatic step.

Reports indicate Syria is considering deploying up to 20,000 troops to Yemen to support Saudi-backed forces against the Houthis. The United States is reportedly not opposed in principle to such a deployment.

Saudi Arabia suffered a direct Houthi strike on Riyadh's international airport, triggering flight suspensions by Lufthansa and Air India. Riyadh and Yemen's internationally recognized government jointly urged the UN Security Council to act amid escalating Houthi attacks.

Lufthansa suspended flights to Riyadh following Houthi airport strikes. Separately, former German spy chief August Hanning faces treason charges linked to his relationship with Israel's former Mossad director.

Iranian operatives were found to have used OpenAI AI models and fake personas to plant anti-US-war stories in multiple American media outlets, per an OpenAI disclosure. Iran-linked forces continued tanker attacks in the Gulf, driving a major oil price surge.

The diplomatic row over two captured North Korean soldiers transferred from Ukraine to South Korea continued to escalate, resulting in Seoul's ambassador recall from Kyiv. North Korean troop involvement in support of Russia's war effort remains the underlying backdrop to the prisoner capture.

financial.notes: Crude oil posted its largest daily gain in approximately one month driven by escalating Iran tanker attacks in the Gulf and hurricane-related production disruptions; US gasoline prices stand at ~$4.30/gallon, up 46% from pre-war levels.

update_log.text: South Korea officially recalls ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW disclosure dispute, confirmed by BBC and multiple outlets.
Al Jazeera UN envoy report confirms Yemen has returned to 'full-scale war' as Houthis escalate strikes on Saudi airports and infrastructure.
Houthi strike on Riyadh airport causes aircraft fire; Lufthansa and Air India suspend Saudi Arabia flights.
Oil prices surge on escalating Iran tanker attacks; US gas prices up 46% from pre-war levels per ABC News.
CNN and OpenAI report Iranian operatives used AI-generated fake personas to plant anti-war disinformation in US media outlets.
Trump rules out new Iran military strike before November 3 US midterm elections, citing ongoing productive talks.
Secretary of State Rubio warns Russia-Ukraine stalemate risks broader regional spillover; urges NATO allies to raise defense spending.
Ukraine strikes Omsk Gazprom Neft refinery — Russia's largest — approximately 2,500 km from the Ukrainian border.
Russian guided bomb kills at least 30 civilians at a bus stop in eastern Ukraine; CBS and Breitbart report 50+ killed in two-day strike wave.
Congressional Budget Office report confirms 81 US aircraft worth up to $3.3 billion lost or damaged in the Iran war, per Al Jazeera.
Russia claims strike on cargo ship delivering supplies to Ukrainian forces at Chernomorsk port.
RT reports Syria weighing deployment of up to 20,000 troops to Yemen in support of Saudi-backed Houthi offensive; US reportedly not opposed.
UNIFIL reports small arms fire targeting Israeli border post in Lebanon; no casualties recorded.
